column2: There are many mysteries in the [Root.Religion.GetName] faith. It might be worth spending some time delving into the old texts of [Root.Religion.GetScriptureName].

There are many mysteries in the [Root.Religion.GetName] religion. It might be worth listening more closely to the ancient stories about [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] told by the [Root.Religion.GetPriestTitle]s.
I will dedicate more time to reading the scriptures.
I shall summon the storytellers.
No, I have no time for this.
For months now you have spent many nights reading [Root.Religion.GetScriptureName]. The texts hold much wisdom, and hint at the deepest mysteries of [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName].

For months now you have spent many nights listening to the old myths of the [Root.Religion.GetName] faith. The tales told of [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName] are stirring, and hold much wisdom for daily life.
These sacred texts illuminate me.
It is wise to listen and ponder.

Your devotion has been noticed across the realm, not least by [From.GetTitledName]. You have written to each other on holy and philosophical matters for some time, and find that you are fast becoming friends.
Our common interests bind us together.

The holy site of [holy_site_visiting.GetName] is a great center of the [Root.Religion.GetName] faith. Many great rites are held there, and the presence of [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName] is said to fill the whole land around it.
I should go!
I can't.
Your visit to [holy_site_visiting.GetName] was well worth the time! You walked its sacred halls and pondered the mysteries hidden there.
Praise [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName]!

I live my life as other [Root.GetMenWomen] do, steering past its rocks and doing my best in all I undertake. Still, everything we do takes place in the sight of [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName], and we must take care lest [Root.Religion.GetRandomEvilGodName] finds a way into our lives.
Indeed it is so.
I should ponder this more deeply.
These holy ponderings give me a headache.

There are those in your realm who worship other gods. [From.GetTitledName], for one, follows the [From.Religion.GetName] cult. You sometimes wonder what [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName] would think of your dealings with such people.
We are more alike than we are different.
Their lesser deities do not interest me.

For a long while now you have not felt [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName] in your thoughts. You begin to wonder whether there is any truth in [Root.Religion.GetScriptureName], or if it is just an old book written by clever liars.
It must be so. [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName] is dead!
These blasphemous feelings will soon pass.
Perish these blasphemous thoughts!
I have spent years studying the tenets of the [Root.Religion.GetName] faith, and by now I count myself a learned [Root.Religion.GetName] scholar.
I will dedicate my life's work to [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName].
Religion has its uses and is well worth the study.
It is interesting, but there are other things in life.
As I prayed before the altar, I was suddenly filled with an overwhelming sense of love. Weeping with joy, I knew that I am never truly alone. [Root.Religion.GetHighGodNameCap] is always with me.

As I cut the throat of the ram, it stopped struggling and looked me straight in the eyes. Even as its blood ran into the grooves of the altar stone, I knew that [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName] was watching me, and was pleased.

At the evening prayer, as the sun sank over the dunes, my mind filled with a vision: the first prophet of [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName], riding a winged steed across the starry sky with a burning sword in hand. It felt more real than waking life...

I stood alone before the ancestor shrine as the forge fires burned low, and for a moment I heard them: the old voices of my line, speaking from the stone itself. My grudges weigh lighter now. The ancestors have not forgotten me.

Me was sittin' by da big rock, all grumpy like, when da sky went green and dis massive green foot came down and stomped right next to me! [Root.Religion.GetHighGodNameCap] is watchin'! Dat means a good scrap is comin'!
I feel renewed!
Yet another morning I wake as tired as when I went to bed. I should do something about my listless mind... Perhaps I need some time alone.
Seclude myself in prayer and meditation.
Bah! I'll get over it eventually.
I have a new respect for the hermits of old! My time fasting and praying in seclusion has done me good. [Root.Religion.GetHighGodNameCap] has helped me strengthen my mind.
Secluded in my cave, I have lived on nothing but the bitter roots and black draughts the priests favour. My thoughts are clear: it is by will alone I set my mind in motion.

Deep in the old halls, with only the drip of water and the cold stone for company, I have counted my grudges and my debts one by one. The ancestors are patient, and in the dark I have learned some of their patience.
Curled up safely in the badger's den, I have steeled my mind against the wailing shadow men who stalk me outside. I wonder how long I have been holed up in here?
Time to cut down on the ale.
Too much food harms the body and dulls the mind.
I have been idle for too long.
Time to set aside my most unhealthy desires.
I must curb my lust.
Praise [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName]! I can see again!
The pox... It's gone! Praise [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName]!
The accursed wailing... is almost quiet now.
I can feel my face again! My leprosy is healed!
My loins are on fire! Praise [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName]!
I resolve to be a better [Root.GetManWoman].

I have come to know [zeal_new_friend.GetTitledName] well these past months. For all that [zeal_new_friend.GetSheHe] prays to other gods, I find we share more than either of us expected: a love of good talk, a dislike of fools, and a suspicion that the priests of both our faiths would be scandalised to see us laughing together.
A friend is a friend, whatever gods [zeal_new_friend.GetSheHe] keeps.

At the feast last night, in my cups and in a temper, I told the whole hall what I think of those who do not follow [Root.Religion.GetName]: heathens, idolaters and fools, every one, and fit only for the pyre. The unbelievers in my realm have heard every word, and they will not soon forget it.
Every word was true!

The ports of Araby are full of Old World merchants, sailors and scholars, and I have dealt with enough of them to know that the followers of Sigmar, Manann and Myrmidia are not the savages our preachers make them out to be. They pray badly, but they pay well, and some of them are even wise.
Let them keep their gods, so long as they keep the peace.
Kill Them All

The walls of [From.GetName] have fallen and my soldiers are pouring into the streets. My captains ask what is to be done with the people: heretics and true believers huddle together in the temples, and no one can tell one from the other.\n\nAn old priest at my side has an answer ready. 'Kill them all,' he says. '[Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName] will know his own.'
Kill them all.
No. Spare those who surrender.
